dicas.texto: Para representar a fração 3/5, em quantas partes iguais precisamos dividir o espaço entre 0 e 1?
Digite o número total de livros no campo 'Number of parts' e clique em OK para ver a reta ser dividida.
O número de partes deve ser igual ao denominador da fração 3/5. Tente inserir 5 no campo 'Number of parts'.
Para dividir a reta corretamente, insira o valor 5 no campo 'Number of parts' e clique no botão OK.
Se a reta está dividida em 5 partes, onde fica a marca que representa a terceira parte?
Conte as divisões partindo do zero. Onde você pararia ao contar três espaços?
Coloque o ponto exatamente na terceira marcação após o zero.
Conte: um, dois, três... marque o ponto na terceira linha vertical que divide a reta.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; as caixas da fração (F1/F2) existem mas a pergunta da fração não é exibida (a fração já está no enunciado); reta numérica de 0 a 1 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto; campo "Number of parts" (denom) + OK que divide a reta em partes iguais (começa em 1); botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, dividir a reta, marcar o ponto, concluir).

componentes.papel: reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico da caixa de baixo da fração (denominador)
campo numérico "Number of parts" + botão OK: divide a reta em partes iguais
botão que registra a fração informada
controle que exibe a etapa de escrever a fração

passos.acao: Enter the denominator of 3/5 in the F2 box.
Enter the number of equal parts and click OK to divide the number line.
Enter the numerator of 3/5 in the F1 box.
Mark the point on the number line that represents the fraction Sally has read.
Click showAnswer to record the fraction represented on the number line.
Click Done to finish the problem with the fraction you recorded.

dicas.texto: Ask yourself whether the denominator describes the part Sally read or the entire assignment.
Look at the bottom number in the fraction and copy it into the F2 box.
The denominator is the number that tells how many books make up the complete assignment.
Use the bottom number of 3/5 in the F2 box, because it represents the complete set of books.
The number line should show one interval for each book in the complete assignment.
Use the total number of books as the number of equal parts, then press OK.
Do not use the number of books already read; use the total needed to complete the assignment.
Type the denominator of the fraction in the Number of parts field, then click OK to create equal intervals.
Ask yourself whether the numerator represents the books already read or the books in the complete assignment.
Look at the top number in the fraction and copy it into the F1 box.
The numerator counts the books Sally has completed so far.
Use the top number of 3/5 in the F1 box, because it counts the completed books.
The point should show the portion completed, measured from zero across the equal intervals.
Start at 0 and move one equal interval for each book Sally has read.
Use the five equal intervals already shown and count only the intervals representing completed books.
Begin at zero, count the completed-book intervals, and place the point at the endpoint of the last counted interval.
Compare the marked point with the halfway point between zero and one.
Read the fraction represented by the marked interval and confirm that it is less than one whole.
The point lies just to the right of one-half, so the fraction is a little greater than one-half.
Use the fraction formed by the completed-book count over the total-book count, then click showAnswer.
Review whether the marked fraction is between one-half and one whole.
Check that the numerator counts completed books and the denominator counts all required books.
Make sure the fraction in the recorded answer matches the point selected on the five-part number line.
Keep the fraction showing the completed portion over the complete assignment, then click Done.

exercicio.statement:
Sally has to read 5 books for her summer assignment. So far, she has read 3 of the books. That is 3/5 of the assignment, and she is convinced that she has read a little more than half of the entire summer assignment. Use the number line to show how much she has read and see if she has actually read a little more than  half of her summer assignment.
-

steps.instruction: Enter the denominator of 3/5 in the F2 box.
Enter the number of equal parts and click OK to divide the number line.
Enter the numerator of 3/5 in the F1 box.
Mark the point on the number line that represents the fraction Sally has read.
Click showAnswer to record the fraction represented on the number line.
Click Done to finish the problem with the fraction you recorded.
